body:
## What to build

Place missing plain-list keys last when a local Margin order is requested, using the row-vector missingness that ordinary local dplyr/vctrs ordering applies. A NULL list element must remain distinct from a nonmissing list element containing a scalar NA.

## Reproduced behavior

On main `bfcdaf76a36d102132cd039c68ba8bc05a4fd465` with R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1 and vctrs 0.7.3, take a two-row tibble whose fixed key is the plain list containing an integer NA element followed by NULL, with payloads 1 and 2. Expansion with that fixed key and the last Margin order returns payloads 2, 1, placing the missing NULL key first. No variable Grouping dimension or occurrence identifier is required.

Ordinary local arrangement returns payloads 1, 2. The vector's missing flags are false, true under vctrs, while scalar `is.na()` returns true, false for the plain list. The Margin missingness term uses that scalar predicate ahead of the otherwise-correct list value order. A classed list-of control follows vctrs missingness and sorts correctly.

Both first and last Margin orders reproduce the error through all four Margin verbs. The detail rows of a rollup expansion over the list dimension reproduce it too; a missing-labelled omitted list dimension is itself represented by NULL. Row counts and copied payloads remain intact.

The Margin-order contract puts missing keys last, including fixed keys. Make the owning decision and reference explicit about plain-list row-vector missingness where needed, preserving the existing packed/matrix and scalar contracts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Plain-list fixed keys containing both NULL and an NA-valued element put NULL last through expansion, summary and both nesting verbs under first and last Margin orders.
- [ ] A typed-missing list Grouping dimension retains correct detail-key order and margin placement.
- [ ] Row counts, source payloads, key types and source objects are preserved; the unsorted option retains its behavior.
- [ ] Classed list-of, packed data-frame, matrix, factor and ordinary scalar controls retain their documented ordering.
- [ ] The public-interface regression asserts missingness and row order, and any necessary clarification lands in the owning Margin-order decision/reference.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

title: [P2] Place NULL plain-list keys last in Margin order
